text.p: NWE oil products firmed on Monday, with gasoline supported by tight supply, traders said.
Gas oil prices ended up to $1 higher in thin volumes in line with a seesawing futures market and underpinned by the impending November contract expiry on Tuesday.
Gasoline rose $5-$6 on heavy buying in the barge market and tighter supplies after the arbitrage opened to the U.S. last week, drawing at least 100,000 tonnes.
Naphtha ended modestly higher on strength in the swaps.
Fuel oil rose up to $5 with crude, but volatile crude which drifted lower, kept physical trades at bay.
